title: Kernel.system calls cause server to stop working
body:
### What version of gRPC and what language are you using?

gRPC >= 1.65.0, Ruby >= ~~3.1.0~~ 3.3.0

### What operating system (Linux, Windows,...) and version?

Various versions of Linux, including containers based on (for example), `ruby:3.X.Y-slim-bullseye`, MacOS (latest).  

### What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g. python version or version of GCC)

MRI

### What did you do?

Unit test: https://github.com/reporter/grpc/commit/e8d7dc32095aa82fe2223c6f0e77a7787e5192ed (line [180](https://github.com/reporter/grpc/commit/e8d7dc32095aa82fe2223c6f0e77a7787e5192ed#diff-d2b230f982304c473c5174c59efa17459047f8359edcf16c792de1e7fc3172cbR180)). 

Literally, any implementation of server handler that is using either `Kernel.system` or [method-i-60](https://ruby-doc.org/core-3.1.1/Kernel.html#method-i-60) methods (e.g.:
```
`echo "test"`
```

If I'm right this behaviour caused by https://github.com/grpc/grpc/commit/d4b5e12f8ecf22b506b2831a4614c62a83458a31 (src/ruby/ext/grpc/rb_completion_queue.c specifically: rolling back those changes get expected/normal behavior back).

### What did you expect to see?

No cancelation in accepting requests, and any system call should not interfere with the server's work.

### What did you see instead?

In the gRPC server any call of `Kernel.system` causes an infinite loop of the next messages:
```
{"time":TIMESTAMP,"level":"WARN","type":"server call failed: request_call completion failed"}
```

The server stops accepting any requests and requires a restart.

### Anything else we should know about your project / environment?

It's crucial sometimes to run something from a shell that is impossible (during regulation, for example, reasons) to reimplement inside the code, and before version `1.65.0` everything works just fine.

UPD: ruby version changed from `>=3.1.0` to `>=3.3.0`

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
You can isolate the system call by running it in a separate thread, preventing it from blocking the main event loop of the gRPC server. This allows the server to continue handling requests without being blocked by the `Kernel.system` call. Here's an example:

```ruby
def run_system_command(command)
  Thread.new do
    Kernel.system(command)
  end
end

class EchoService < EchoService::Service
  def Echo(request, call)
    run_system_command("echo 'test'")  # Use thread to prevent blocking
    call.send_response(EchoResponse.new(message: "Test complete"))
  end
end
```
By doing this, the system command will be executed in the background, and the main thread (which is handling the gRPC calls) will not be blocked.

Cheers,
participant1

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thank you, @participant1! I appreciate your help. Your suggested method would work if we didn’t need to capture the result of the system/shell call. Unfortunately, as long as the thread needs to remain synchronized in any form, the issue inevitably reappears. (Just to clarify, this behavior occurs only in gRPC versions 1.65 and above.)

Please correct me if I’m wrong, but the test results suggest that threads won’t resolve the issue. 😔

Thanks again!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2 Thank you for your response!
You can easily reproduce the issue by using a server definition like this:
```ruby
# GreeterServer is simple server that implements the Helloworld Greeter server.
class GreeterServer < Helloworld::Greeter::Service
  # say_hello implements the SayHello rpc method.
  def say_hello(hello_req, _unused_call)
    Kernel.system('echo "test"')
    Helloworld::HelloReply.new(message: "Hello #{hello_req.name}")
  end
end
```
Please note that to run this, I had to recompile the proto files. Without recompiling, [this file](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/examples/ruby/lib/helloworld_pb.rb) causes 
```
undefined method `build' for an instance of Google::Protobuf::DescriptorPool` for the version of gRPC >= `1.65.0`).
```

With the above server definition, the server responds to the first call like this: (for a client)
```
"Greeting: Hello world"
WARNING: All log messages before absl::InitializeLog() is called are written to STDERR
I0000 00:00:1736639275.158268   22732 chttp2_transport.cc:1204] ipv6:%5B::1%5D:50051: Got goaway [2] err=UNAVAILABLE:GOAWAY received; Error code: 2; Debug Text: Cancelling all calls {created_time:"2025-01-11T23:47:55.158266722+00:00", http2_error:2, grpc_status:14
```
For version `1.69.0`, the first call does not show any issues on the server side. However, the second call fails, and the client responds with:
```
bundle exec ./greeter_client.rb 
ERROR: 14:failed to connect to all addresses; last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:127.0.0.1:50051: Failed to connect to remote host: Connection refused. debug_error_string:{UNKNOWN:Error received from peer  {created_time:"2025-01-11T23:50:39.259592739+00:00", grpc_status:14, grpc_message:"failed to connect to all addresses; last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:127.0.0.1:50051: Failed to connect to remote host: Connection refused"}}
```
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f92f7449-f9ed-4325-b714-e91c97248422)

If needed, I can provide a repository, but it is essentially a mirror of the [current example](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/tree/master/examples/ruby) folder.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
aha, yes I can repro *with* ruby-3.4  (FWIW I could not repro with ruby 3.2)

With a cursory look https://github.com/grpc/grpc/commit/d4b5e12f8ecf22b506b2831a4614c62a83458a31 definitely looks related.

That commit changed our `rb_thread_call_without_gvl` "unblocking func" to itself initiate server shutdown.

Likely something changed in a ruby 3.X version that triggers `rb_thread_call_without_gvl` unblocking func to run when we shell out (e.g. perhaps b/c of a signal for the child process).

We were probably "getting away with this" before that grpc patch, by taking [this code path](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/b64756acca2eb942c97a416850ce5ab95a544d3e/src/ruby/lib/grpc/generic/rpc_server.rb#L474) to avoid server shutdown.

I'll try to take a deeper look later this week.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Sorry for the delay here. Still haven't been able to give attention to this.

Quick summary of where this is at though:

Note, ideally we could just revert https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/36916, but that itself is a fix forward for another issue that can cause a thread to hang indefinitely upon process shutdown).

But, now that Event Engine has been enabled (ref https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/c68886d1c5e9a4014523ead76bc1224ed94560d7/src/core/lib/experiments/rollouts.yaml#L57 and other `event_engine_` experiments), we can probably go ahead and remove the aforementioned [thread](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/c68886d1c5e9a4014523ead76bc1224ed94560d7/src/ruby/ext/grpc/rb_channel.c#L780) entirely (we need to confirm the EE experiment is rollback safe, though).

After that thread is removed, then we could do a small revert to go back to the `completion_queue_pluck` behavior that we had before https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/36916 (i.e. go back to the timer-based polling loop we had earlier).

Then, grpc would be fixed for these new ruby versions.

----------------

Separately, the newer ruby behavior with spurious invocations of the unblocking func for [rb_thread_call_without_gvl](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/blob/4646ab89179aa3dac917a16aaa16533548ad33d9/thread.c#L1592C4-L1592C30) still *feels* like an issue (unless I'm missing something). If that could end up being fixed, then we could keep the behavior from https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/36916 around.
